subject: art-and-design
topicName: Art Craft and Design Making Connections

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Art explores ideas and personal expression; craft emphasises making, skill and material knowledge; design responds to needs, briefs and function.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Art, Craft and Design title requires working in at least TWO different disciplines — this breadth is a STRENGTH, not a complication.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Cross-disciplinary approaches create richer work: painting informed by textile techniques; photography combined with printmaking; 3D design with graphic communication.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Your portfolio must show both BREADTH (multiple disciplines) and DEPTH (sustained development in each area), connected by a coherent theme.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring art craft and design making connections. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with art craft and design making connections. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with art craft and design making connections. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to art craft and design making connections, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to  | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
